clue.text: In other words, they wrecked a cutter

parts.note: SC abbreviates scilicet, Latin for 'namely', i.e. 'in other words'

indicators.note: wrecked says the letters of the word they are smashed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Put another way, a gang smashed up a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrecked' scrambles the pronoun after the abbreviation. 'cutter' looks like a boat but is a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved blade on a pole used to mow grass is a cutting tool.

clue.text: Ornament, of course

explanation.surface: Decoration, naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: To engrave metal is to decorate it in this way, and to course hares is to pursue them, another sense of the same verb.

clue.text: Presume to say good-bye

explanation.surface: Someone takes it upon themselves to bid farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both to take a liberty (as in taking leave to differ) and to bid farewell when departing.

clue.text: Colleague turns up — but not the right entrance

indicators.note: not says a letter is dropped from what has been built
in a down clue, turns up says the word for colleague is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: a colleague is a partner

explanation.surface: A co-worker arrives, but uses the wrong door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' gives RENTRAP; 'not' then drops the R. 'entrance' is the verb (to bewitch, ensnare), not a doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to captivate them, catching them as in a snare.

clue.text: It's touching when, an entertainer gets a little money

parts.note: a DJ (disc jockey) is an entertainer
a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: It is heartwarming when a performer earns a few pennies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touching' looks emotional but means physically next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Things next to each other, sharing a border, are said to be adjoining or in contact.

clue.text: Father had potato mashed without delay

indicators.note: mashed, as potatoes are, says these three words are pulped and their letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad made himself mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means instantly, with no hesitation at all.

clue.text: Name boat after a fish

parts.note: John is a common man's name
a dory is a small flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: Christen a vessel in honour of a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-bodied edible sea fish with a dark spot on each side.

clue.text: Here we'll be in insular surroundings

indicators.note: be in says the we goes inside the island's name

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is a Greek island, so it gives island letters to surround
we'll is read as 'we will', supplying we

explanation.surface: We will be staying here on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be in' signals the insertion. 'Here' works as the definition because the town is a sailing centre on the Isle of Wight, so 'insular' fits the whole clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A port town on an island off England's south coast is the place 'here' points to.

clue.text: Don't worry about unpleasant people, Edward

indicators.note: about says the name for Edward goes round the nasty folk

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
vermin are obnoxious people

explanation.surface: Someone tells Edward not to fret over horrible people.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said to tell someone to forget it and not be concerned.

clue.text: Supports little chap by sewing

parts.note: to back is to support
titch is British slang for a small person

explanation.surface: Someone props up a small man by doing needlework.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong hand stitch in which each stitch doubles back over the last is a kind of needlework.

clue.text: Give up without one flourish

indicators.note: without says a letter is removed

parts.note: to waive a right is to give it up
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Stop doing it, minus one bit of showiness.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish a sword or hand is to brandish it with a sweeping movement.

clue.text: Revealing Rossini's libretto?

explanation.surface: Something giving away a secret about an opera's words.
explanation.walkthrough: Rossini wrote the opera William Tell, so its libretto is cryptically Tell's story.
explanation.definitionFit: A giveaway sign is revealing, and Rossini's opera libretto tells the story of William Tell.

clue.text: What a waste to quit the Army!

explanation.surface: A deserter wasting his military career.
explanation.definitionFit: An arid wasteland is a desert, and a soldier who abandons service is said to desert.

clue.text: It's essential to laugh a happy laugh

indicators.note: It's essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Laughing heartily is vital.
explanation.definitionFit: The reduplicated syllable is how laughter is written down.

clue.text: Hit back it could become excessive.

indicators.note: could become says these letters may be turned into something else by rearranging

explanation.surface: Retaliating might be overdoing things.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means unreasonable or more than is fair.

clue.text: An uncommon sight — two artists with one girl

parts.note: RA (Royal Academician) is the usual abbreviation for an artist, taken twice
RA (Royal Academician) is the usual abbreviation for an artist, taken twice
Avis is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A rare spectacle: a pair of painters escorting a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: RA twice, then AVIS, a girl's name. The Latin phrase means 'rare bird'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for a rare bird is used for any exceptional rarity.

clue.text: City road

explanation.surface: An urban street.
explanation.definitionFit: Alaska's largest city has this name, and a road (roadstead) is a sheltered place where ships can lie at anchor.

clue.text: Bloke bit baboon

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a bit is a drill, the boring tool

explanation.surface: A man was bitten by a monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the past tense of bite but is the noun, a drill bit.
explanation.definitionFit: This large West African primate with a colourful face is a kind of baboon.

clue.text: Fred, Pam and I could make an explosive mixture

indicators.note: could make says the three names' letters can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Three friends might cook up something that blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: Methane gas that collects in coal mines forms an explosive mix with air.

clue.text: Buffalo Bill retiring about Dec 1st

indicators.note: about says the shy word goes round the next letter

parts.note: a retiring person is shy, coy

indicators.note: 1st says only the first letter of Dec is taken

explanation.surface: A Wild West showman going into retirement around the start of December.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like giving up work but means shy; D goes inside COY.
explanation.definitionFit: William Frederick Cody was the Wild West showman known by that nickname.

clue.text: Knocker it's in a lot of pain

indicators.note: in says it goes inside the shortened pain
a lot of says most of the word for pain is kept, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a crick is a painful muscle spasm
it's is read as 'it is', supplying it

explanation.surface: A door knocker is suffering badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' cuts CRICK to CRIC, and IT goes 'in' it. 'Knocker' is slang for someone who disparages.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who knocks things, finding fault, is a reviewer or fault-finder.

clue.text: Put on weight, and looked older

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, a British unit of weight (14 pounds)
aged means grew or looked older

explanation.surface: Someone gained weight and seemed older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on weight' reads as one phrase but 'Put on' is the definition, as a play is put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A play that has been put on has been produced or mounted.

clue.text: Leave one's bed and dress

explanation.surface: Rising and getting dressed in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise from sleep is to get out of bed, and an outfit, especially an odd one, is called a getup.

clue.text: Certainly: out, therefore nothing comes in

indicators.note: comes in says the pieces for therefore and nothing go inside the word for out

parts.note: forth means out, as in 'go forth'
so means therefore
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Sure: the result is that nothing gets in from outside.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic exclamation meaning truly or indeed.

clue.text: Canines, perhaps, that eat everything they have put in front of them

indicators.note: put in front of them says the letters at the front of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Dogs that will eat anything you set before them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canines' suggests dogs, but these canines are pointed teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are one kind of the hard biting structures in the mouth, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Invent a bomb

explanation.surface: Someone devises an explosive device.
explanation.definitionFit: To coin a new word or phrase is to invent it, and a bomb is British slang for a fortune, a large sum.

clue.text: Characters who aren't with it are for it

indicators.note: characters means the letters of these words are used in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: People who are out of touch are bound to get into trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. 'for it' is the idiom 'in for it', facing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in trouble, facing punishment, is the sense of being 'for it'.

clue.text: Look in heaven and hell for the man of God

parts.note: the sky is the heavens

indicators.note: in says the word for look sits inside the word for hell

parts.note: the pit is hell
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Search heaven and hell for a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Sky pilot is old slang for a chaplain or clergyman.

clue.text: Children are left here to crib

explanation.surface: Kids are dropped off to copy.
explanation.definitionFit: A day nursery is where children are left, and a crib is a nativity scene, which the French word also names.
